issues.detail: Instructions cover happy-path scenarios and include a Common Pitfalls section, but lack error handling patterns in the main Steps (e.g., handling missing/invalid API keys, dataset creation failures, network timeouts, rate limiting).
Skill claims Python 3.10+ or Node.js 18+ support and mentions npm install, but all runnable examples are Python-only; Node.js users must infer TypeScript translations without concrete code samples.

scenarios.name: setup-qa-bot-with-evaluation
scenarios.rationale: Response A correctly sets LANGSMITH_TRACING and LANGSMITH_API_KEY as specified in the rubric, defines three evaluators, and demonstrates evaluate() integration with clean code; Response B fails the primary requirement by using incorrect LANGCHAIN_* environment variable names instead of LANGSMITH_*, additionally uses outdated callback patterns, and neither response fully demonstrates actual trace output structure with metadata tags.

scenarios.name: monitor-production-latency-and-errors
scenarios.rationale: Response A comprehensively demonstrates client.list_runs() with multiple complete examples, correct filter syntax (eq, gte, gt operators), and extraction of all three required metrics (latency_ms, error, total_tokens) with aggregations; Response B focuses on instrumentation setup and provides minimal API examples, lacks token count extraction entirely, and does not show programmatic extraction of metrics from run objects.

scenarios.name: custom-evaluator-from-production-traces
scenarios.rationale: Response B directly implements the rubric requirements using create_dataset(), create_examples() with 'inputs'/'outputs' keys, and defines evaluators with the correct signature (outputs, reference_outputs) returning {key, score} dicts, then runs evaluate(); Response A uses a completely different framework (Anthropic SDK with manual JSON) and never calls any of the specified functions.
